people.name: Tunde
people.description: British singer and songwriter of Nigerian descent Tunde Baiyewu, who with the Lighthouse Family, had the 1996 UK No.4 single 'Lifted' plus 9 other UK Top 40 singles. Their 1995 debut album Ocean Drive sold more than 1.8 million copies in the UK alone.

people.name: Rodney Sheppard
people.description: Rodney Sheppard is the guitarist for the American rock band Sugar Ray. In 1997, the group attained mainstream success with the pop-infused single 'Fly'. Their top-selling album, 14:59, came out in 1999.

people.name: Stacey Lattishaw
people.description: American R&B singer Stacey Lattishaw, who had the 1980 US No.21 single 'Let Me Be Your Angel' and the 1980 UK No.3 single 'Jump to The Beat'. She signed with Motown in 1986. She scored her only No. 1 R&B hit with duet partner Johnny Gill, titled 'Where Do We Go from Here', in 1989.

people.name: Fernando and Nefty Sallaberry
people.description: Fernando and Nefty Sallaberry are singers and actors who belonged to the original lineup of the Puerto Rican boy band Menudo. Menudo has been ranked among the biggest boy bands of all time, with worldwide album sales estimated at 20 million.

people.name: Tim Armstrong
people.description: American musician, songwriter, and record producer Tim Armstrong is recognized for his unique voice and serves as the singer and guitarist for the punk rock band Rancid alongside the hip-hop and punk rock supergroup Transplants. Beyond his primary bands, Armstrong writes songs for various other musicians. His professional collaborations include working with Joe Walsh and the Interrupters, and he earned a Grammy Award for his contributions to the work of Jimmy Cliff and Pink.

people.name: Mark Lanegan
people.description: Mark Lanegan was an American alternative rock musician and singer-songwriter. He co-founded Screaming Trees and belonged to Queens of the Stone Age, appearing on five of their albums. Lanegan passed away on 22 February 2022 at the age of 57.

people.name: Amy Grant
people.description: American singer-songwriter and musician Amy Grant achieved a 1991 US No.1 and UK No.2 single with 'Baby Baby'. By 2009, she had sold over 30 million albums globally and earned six Grammy Awards along with 22 Gospel Music Association Dove Awards. Additionally, Grant released the first Christian album to achieve platinum status.

people.name: Steve Rothery
people.description: Steve Rothery is the guitarist of the British rock band Marillion, known for the 1985 UK No.2 single 'Kayleigh'. Between 1983 and 1994, the group secured eight Top Ten UK albums, which included the 1985 No.1 album Misplaced Childhood.

people.name: Jocelyn Brown
people.description: Jocelyn Brown is an American R&B and dance singer. She landed a No.5 single in the UK in 1997 with 'Something Goin' On' and has collaborated with John Lennon, Bob Dylan, and Bruce Springsteen. Her vocals have featured on 23 hit singles on the UK singles chart, including eight entries that made the top 20.

people.name: Bev Bevan
people.description: English rock musician and Electric Light Orchestra drummer Bev Bevan previously played for The Move, scoring the 1969 UK No.1 single 'Blackberry Way'. Alongside his work with Electric Light Orchestra—which included the 1979 UK No.3 and US No.4 single 'Don't Bring Me Down' as well as 26 other Top 40 hits—Bevan also performed as the touring drummer for Black Sabbath during their 1983 Born Again Tour.

people.name: Bob Lind
people.description: Bob Lind is an American playwright, novelist, and singer-songwriter who helped define the 1960s folk rock movement in the US and UK. His single 'Elusive Butterfly' became a No.5 hit in both the US and the UK in 1966.

people.name: Percy Sledge
people.description: Percy Sledge was an American R&B, soul and gospel singer. In 1966, he released the single 'When A Man Loves A Woman', which reached No. 1 in the US and No. 4 in the UK. His career experienced a renaissance during the 1980s when the track returned to the UK Singles Chart following its feature in a Levi's commercial, climbing to No. 2 behind a reissue of Ben E. King's classic 'Stand by Me'. Sledge was married twice and fathered twelve children. He passed away from liver cancer on April 14th 2015.

works.title: Fame
works.eventDescription: American singer and actress Irene Cara passed away at age 63 due to hypertensive and arteriosclerotic heart disease. She gained widespread recognition playing Coco Hernandez in the 1980 musical film Fame and by performing its title track 'Fame', which secured the No. 1 position on charts across multiple nations. During 1983, Cara performed and co-authored 'Flashdance... What a Feeling' for the movie Flashdance, earning a shared Academy Award for Best Original Song alongside a Grammy Award for Best Female Pop Vocal Performance in 1984. Initially selected as a dancer for Fame, producers Alan Marshall and David Da Silva adjusted the part of Coco Hernandez specifically for her after discovering her vocal abilities.

works.title: Sailing
works.eventDescription: Scottish singer-songwriter Iain Sutherland, co-writer of Sir Rod Stewart's 1975 hit 'Sailing', has passed away. Sutherland originally recorded the track with his brother Gavin in 1972 prior to its international success under Sir Rod. Initially performing together as the folk group Sutherland Brothers Band, the siblings subsequently merged with a local rock outfit named Quiver to form Sutherland Brothers & Quiver.

works.title: Blood on the Tracks
works.eventDescription: Don DeVito, a longtime Columbia Records executive who produced the key Bob Dylan albums Blood on the Tracks and Desire, passed away at the age of 72 following a 16-year fight against prostate cancer. Throughout his career, DeVito also collaborated with performers such as Bruce Springsteen, Billy Joel, and Aerosmith. His career began as a touring guitarist for Al Kooper, and he previously led his own group, The Sabres, which dissolved during a tour. Columbia stated that DeVito was left stranded in Fort Smith, Ark., when a chance meeting with Johnny Cash sparked a lifelong friendship, with Cash eventually introducing DeVito to Dylan.

works.title: Cum on Feel the Noize
works.eventDescription: Kevin Dubrow, the frontman with metal band Quiet Riot, was found dead in his Las Vegas home at the age of 52. Their 1983 release Metal Health was the first metal album to top the US charts. The band's biggest hit was 'Cum on Feel the Noize', a cover of the Slade song which they are said to have grudgingly recorded in just one take.

works.title: Confessions on a Dance Floor
works.eventDescription: Madonna earned her sixth No. 1 on the US album charts, marking her third consecutive chart-topping album in the US, with 'Confessions on a Dance Floor'. Setting a new record, the album reached No. 1 across 40 countries. This record was previously held by The Beatles, whose album 1 went to No. 1 in 36 countries in 2000 The Beatles.

works.title: Rhinestone Cowboy
works.eventDescription: Glen Campbell was taken into custody in Phoenix, Arizona, following a collision between his BMW and a Toyota Camry, registering a blood alcohol level of .20. The charges against him included 'extreme' drunk driving, hit and run, and assaulting an officer of the law. According to a police report, Campbell continuously hummed his successful track 'Rhinestone Cowboy' while he was being held.

works.title: Swing When You're Winning
works.eventDescription: Robbie Williams began an eight-week tenure at No. 1 on the UK album chart with Swing When You're Winning. The release achieved a 7x Platinum certification, remained on the UK Albums Chart for 57 weeks, and secured the position of the 49th best-selling album in UK history.

works.title: Exhale (Shoop Shoop)
works.eventDescription: Whitney Houston achieved a US singles chart No. 1 with "Exhale (Shoop Shoop)". Composed by Babyface and featured in the movie "Waiting To Exhale", the track marked her 11th US No. 1.

works.title: Do They Know It’s Christmas?
works.eventDescription: British pop stars assembled at S.A.R.M. Studios in London to record the historic single "Do They Know It's Christmas?". Midge Ure and Bob Geldof wrote the track, which included performances by Paul Young, Boy George, Bono, Sting, and George Michael. The release surpassed three million sales in the UK to become the bestselling record of all time, while generating more than £8 million ($13.6 million) globally.

works.title: Pink Moon
works.eventDescription: UK singer and songwriter Nick Drake passed away in his sleep at the age of 26 following an overdose of the antidepressant tryptasol. Having signed with Island Records at the age of twenty, Drake recorded the 1972 album Pink Moon. Volkswagen used the title track from Pink Moon in a TV commercial in 2000, leading Drake to sell more records within a single month than he had over the preceding thirty years.

works.title: My Ding a-Ling
works.eventDescription: Chuck Berry topped the UK singles chart with 'My Ding a-Ling', which marked his sole No.1 single in the UK. Originally, Dave Bartholomew recorded the track in 1952. The recording of Berry's version took place during a concert on 3 February 1972 at the Locarno ballroom in Coventry, England. Jim Connors, a disc jockey for Boston radio station WMEX, received a gold record for finding the song and driving it to the top of the charts through radio airplay and his influence among American peers.

works.title: Cold Turkey
works.eventDescription: John Lennon sent his MBE back to The Queen, citing Britain's part in the Nigeria-Biafra conflict, American actions in Vietnam, and the downward chart movement of his newest single, 'Cold Turkey'.

works.title: The Carnival Is Over
works.eventDescription: The Seekers achieved a No. 1 hit on the UK singles chart with 'The Carnival Is Over', which marked their second chart-topper. The track originated as an 1883 Russian folk song and features lyrics penned by Tom Springfield, the brother of Dusty Springfield. During its highest sales period, the single moved 93,000 copies daily and currently holds the No. 30 spot among the best-selling singles in United Kingdom history.

works.title: Hoot's Mon!
works.eventDescription: Lord Rockinghams XI were at No.1 on the UK singles chart with 'Hoot's Mon', (based on the traditional Scottish folk song 'One Hundred Pipers'). Lord Rockingham's XI were the house band on the UK Jack Good TV show 'Oh Boy.'
